ev.manumission.note.E03: Roman slaves could keep personal savings (peculium) and buy their freedom. Freedmen became citizens, though with limits; their children were born with full rights.
ev.y_goat_kid.text.E03: The goat had twins, and the weakest kid was given to you to raise. Now it follows you everywhere and chews the hem of your tunic.
ev.y_master_son_nuts.text.E03: While no one was looking, you played at nuts with the master's son. He lost and didn't even mind - then his nurse came and led him away without a glance at you.
ev.y_knucklebones.text.E03: You won a whole handful of knucklebones from the neighborhood kids. The secret is simple: throw with a twist and hold your breath.
ev.y_hoop.text.E03: You were driving a bronze hoop with jingling rings down the street and knocked over a basket of figs at the corner. The fruit seller chased you for two blocks.
ev.y_potter_father.text.E03: {npc}, your father, sat you down at the potter's wheel. Your bowl came out as lopsided as a drunken satyr, but he fired it in the kiln anyway and put it on the shelf.
ev.y_nickname.text.2.E03: For your love of boiled chickpeas they started calling you Chickpea. You don't mind: chickpeas are a fine thing.
ev.y_wax_tablet.text.E03: You scratched letters into a wax tablet with a stylus while the teacher paced between the benches with his cane. At least you can rub out a mistake with the blunt end - unlike in life.
ev.y_friend_caught.wriggle.success.E03: You left the vendor holding a scrap of your tunic and vanished down an alley.
ev.y_runaway_thanks.friendship.E03: Invite him for a cup of wine
ev.y_first_job.fuller.E03: At the fuller's - tread wool in the vats
ev.y_first_job.text.E03: The neighbors are looking for someone to do odd jobs for a couple of coins a day. There are two offers, and each one smells in its own way.
ev.y_sibling_quarrel.text.E03: The amphora of oil lies in pieces. Father asks who did it, and {npc} silently looks at you. You both knocked it over, fighting for the last fig.
ev.y_sibling_remembers.text.E03: At the festive table {npc} suddenly brings up that broken amphora - in front of everyone, laughing. But {g=npc_sex:his|her} eyes aren't laughing.
ev.c_first_steps.text.E03: Your {g=npc_sex:son|daughter} {npc} took {g=npc_sex:his|her} first steps: three steps from the hearth straight to you - then sat down hard, looking as if that had been the plan all along. The whole household clapped as if at the games.
ev.c_broken_amphora.laugh.E03: Laugh - the wine was turning anyway
ev.c_broken_amphora.text.E03: Your {g=npc_sex:son|daughter} {npc} broke the amphora of your best wine and blamed the cat. The cat sits nearby, radiating contempt.
ev.c_honest_later.text.E03: They say {npc} refused to short-weigh a customer, even when told to. The boss was furious - and now that customer deals with no one else. You remember a broken amphora and a cat.
ev.c_fear_dark.text.E03: Your {g=npc_sex:son|daughter} {npc} is afraid of the dark: the old woman next door told stories of Lamia, who steals naughty children. Now a lamp burns by the bed all night, and the oil goes as if it were a festival.
ev.c_mischief.text.3.E03: Your {g=npc_sex:son|daughter} {npc} traded your best sandals for a handful of nuts and a dead beetle. Both parties consider the deal fair - everyone except you.
ev.c_river.thank.ok.E03: The fisherman left with a jug of wine. You went on flinching at the word "river" for a long time.
ev.c_child_fall.text.E03: Your {g=npc_sex:son|daughter} {npc} climbed the old olive tree by the road and fell. The arm is swollen and hangs wrong. {g=npc_sex:He|She} is trying very hard not to cry.
ev.c_lost.text.E03: At the festival your {g=npc_sex:son|daughter} {npc} got lost in the crowd. You spent half the day rushing round the market - and found the runaway by the temple, front row, mouth open, listening to a storyteller.
ev.c_knucklebones.text.E03: Your {g=npc_sex:son|daughter} {npc} beat you at knucklebones five times running. On the sixth you noticed {g=npc_sex:his|her} bones were suspiciously obedient.
ev.c_teacher.home_teach.ok.E03: In the evenings the two of you sit over the tablet. You've discovered you'd long forgotten half the letters yourself.
ev.c_teacher.new_teacher.ok.E03: The new teacher teaches letters with honey biscuits: learn your alpha, eat your alpha. Lessons are going well.
ev.c_teacher.teacher.ok.E03: There's more tablet work at home now. {npc} grumbles, but the letters have got straighter.
ev.c_talent.lessons.ok.E03: Now lyre practice drifts from the house every evening. The neighbors are split between the enchanted and the exhausted.
ev.c_figs.defend.E03: Stand up for {g=npc_sex:him|her}: half his figs rot anyway
ev.c_figs.defend.ok.E03: The neighbor left, cursing loud enough for the whole block. {npc} looks at you like a hero, and you ate the figs together.
ev.c_figs.dinner.E03: Invite the neighbor to dinner - figs included
ev.c_figs.dinner.failure.E03: The neighbor didn't see the funny side and left, slamming the door. He did leave the figs, though.
ev.c_figs.pay.ok.E03: For three days {npc} weeded the neighbor's beds. {g=npc_sex:He|She} can't stand the sight of figs now.
ev.c_figs.text.E03: Your {g=npc_sex:son|daughter} {npc} came home with a lap full of figs - and the neighbor right behind, holding the little thief by the ear and demanding justice.
ev.c_rebellion.text.E03: For the third night running your {g=npc_sex:son|daughter} {npc} has come home near dawn, smelling of wine and talking back: "I'm not a child anymore!" The neighbors saw {g=npc_sex:him|her} with company best not mentioned.
ev.c_trade.scribe.ok.E03: {npc} now carries wax tablets under one arm and looks at you a little condescendingly: you, after all, can't spell.
ev.c_trade_high.estates.ok.E03: {npc} rides round the estates, counting olive trees and arguing with the stewards. The stewards already miss the old days.
ev.c_trade_high.text.E03: Your {g=npc_sex:son|daughter} {npc} has grown up. Friends advise: serving the gods brings honor, Greek medicine brings respect and income, the family estates bring security. The choice is yours - but {npc} already has opinions.
ev.c_wedding.lavish.ok.E03: Flute girls, torches, a mountain of honey cakes. The street talked about this wedding until the next one.
ev.c_wedding_debt_later.pay.ok.E03: You counted out the coins and, for the first time in years, breathed easy.
ev.c_far_away.bless.ok.E03: You stood on the shore until the sail was a dot. The house has become far too quiet.
ev.c_far_away.text.E03: Your {g=npc_sex:son|daughter} {npc} wants to leave: {g=npc_sex:sign on with a trading ship or the army and see the world|go with her husband to a distant colony where his family has a business}. Promises to come back rich. You recall that everyone promises that.
ev.c_debts_again.cut.E03: Say it: not one more coin
ev.c_business_bad.comfort.ok.E03: You poured some wine and told {g=npc_sex:him|her} about your own failures. There turned out to be a surprising number.
ev.c_grand_spoil.build.E03: Instead of buying one - build the chariot together
ev.c_grand_spoil.build.ok.E03: The chariot came out crooked, but it's theirs. {npc} shows it to everyone: "{g:Grandpa|Grandma} and me made it!"
ev.c_grand_spoil.spoil.ok.E03: The chariot is hidden under your bed, and the cake was eaten on the spot. It's your shared secret.
ev.c_grand_spoil.text.E03: Your {g=npc_sex:grandson|granddaughter} {npc} whispers a request for a honey cake - and a toy chariot. The parents have strictly forbidden spoiling.
ev.c_grand_craft_later.text.E03: {npc} is nearly grown and makes things better than you do. One day {g=npc_sex:he|she} admitted it all started with that crooked chariot the two of you built.
ev.c_h_wound.honey.E03: Wash it with wine and dress it with honey, as the old folks did
ev.c_h_wound.honey.success.E03: Wine, honey, a clean cloth twice a day. The wound closed - the old folks knew what they were doing.
ev.c_h_wound.temple.E03: Take a clay arm to the temple - that's how you ask the gods for healing
ev.c_h_wound.temple.failure.E03: There are hundreds of clay arms in the temple. Yours evidently hasn't come up yet.
ev.c_h_wound.temple.success.E03: The clay arm now hangs in the temple among hundreds of others. Your real one has healed.
ev.c_h_wound.text.E03: A trifling scratch from a rusty nail has swollen and reddened in a week and throbs so hard you can't sleep. Your arm is hot right up to the elbow.
ev.c_h_stomach.barley.E03: Fast and drink barley water, as physicians advise
ev.c_h_stomach.barley.failure.E03: The barley water didn't help. The sickness hangs on and wears you down to the bone.
ev.c_h_stomach.barley.success.E03: Three days on barley water and your stomach settled. The first flatbread afterwards tasted like a feast.
ev.c_h_cough.text.E03: The cough has hung on since winter and has no intention of leaving: at night your chest feels stuffed with wool. The physician shakes his head and advises what he advises all wealthy patients - a sea voyage and dry air.
ev.c_h_cough.voyage.ok.E03: A month on deck, salt wind, the dry sun of foreign shores. You came back without the cough and with a pile of stories.
ev.c_h_tooth.endure.E03: Rinse with vinegar and grit your teeth
ev.c_h_tooth.physician.success.E03: The physician let out the pus, rinsed the gum with wine and left the tooth in place. You chewed with it for many more years.
ev.c_h_plague.stay.E03: Stay: fumigate the house, wash with vinegar, keep away from the harbor
ev.c_h_plague.text.E03: At the harbor they talk of a ship where half the rowers died of fever. Two people in the next quarter have already taken to their beds. The city whispers, and every cough sounds like a sentence.
ev.c_h_still_ill.physician.ok.E03: The physician changed the draughts, forbade wine and ordered sleep until noon. Two weeks later you were up.
ev.c_h_family_doctor.accept.ok.E03: Now once a month the physician takes your pulse, looks at your tongue and eyes the wine disapprovingly. It costs money - and, it seems, buys years.
ev.c_h_family_doctor.text.E03: A Greek physician who has treated your neighbors makes an offer: for a regular fee he'll look after the whole family - take pulses, advise on food and come at the first call.
ev.c_h_gym_invite.decline.ok.E03: {g:The trainer|She} shrugged. So did you, and went off to lunch.
ev.c_h_gym_invite.text.E03: {g:A trainer from the palaestra|The keeper of a bathhouse with an exercise yard} looks you up and down: "Stooped shoulders, soft belly. Come to us - {g:running, wrestling, oil and strigil|ball games, light weights and oil rubs}. In a year you won't recognize yourself."
ev.c_h_gym_invite.walks.ok.E03: You decided to go everywhere on foot - to the river, to the market, out of town. Free, and no strigil required.
ev.c_h_diet.feast.ok.E03: The physician left, shaking his head. The wine was excellent.
ev.c_h_diet.text.E03: A Greek physician you know watched you eat and delivered a whole lecture: less fatty meat and unmixed wine, more barley, greens and walking. "Moderation in all things," he concluded.
ev.c_h_gout_later.diet.ok.E03: Without wine and meat life has gone bland and the foot has gone well. You keep haggling with yourself over which matters more.
ev.c_h_aging.text.2.E03: You have to hold the scroll farther and farther from your eyes. Soon, apparently, you'll need longer arms.
ev.c_h_back.baths.E03: Go to the baths every day
ev.c_h_back.baths.ok.E03: The hot room, the cold pool, the masseur's hands - your back straightened, and you caught up on all the city gossip besides.
ev.c_h_back.text.E03: Your back has seized up so badly you can't straighten. Friends recommend the masseur at the baths - he'll knead you, steam you, rub you with oil. The family recommends lying down and not moving.
ev.c_h_quack.text.E03: A trader at the market shouts that his potion cures fever, baldness, toothache and unrequited love. You didn't buy any, but you enjoyed listening - the show was better than the theater.
